newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finland Bank seen buying markka for marks -dealers.
newsitem.headline: Finland Bank seen buying markka for marks -dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Finland was seen intervening in the foreign exchange market on Friday, buying markka for marks in an attempt to halt a sharp weakening of the markka, forex dealers said.
"They have been in three times, last time at 3.02. But the markka is still weakening," a senior dealer said.

The markka has softened this week as big overseas investors, who had bought substantial amounts of markka in January, were now pulling out of the Finnish currency, selling big amounts of markka for marks, dealers said.
A senior official at the Bank of Finland's market intervention department declined comment, in line with the central bank's standard policy.
A dealer said the Bank of Finland was not trying to prevent the markka from weakening, but rather carrying out its stated policy of cushioning excessively big intra-day moves in the exchange rate.

At 1100/0800 GMT, the markka traded at 3.0290 per German mark -- its weakest since September 1996. On Thursday, DEM/FIM closed at 3.0060. It opened in Helsinki at 3.0180. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
